ops-bot: INCIDENT 2 — detected repeated container restarts on gpu-cluster-12; reason=fatal OOM during prefill for long-session workloads. Pager routed to @maya :rotating_light:
maya: picking this up, joining bridge now. who else is seeing the same traces?
jamie: I see it — model-serving-prod/v2 on node gpu-12 restarted 5x in last 6m. CrashLoopBackOff. Logs show OOM in prefill op when sequence length > 120k tokens.
jamie: relevant log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Allocated=23.4G, Active=23.4G, Reserved=24.0G, Total=48.0G
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/runtime/inference.py", line 412, in prefill_loop
    kv_cache.extend(new_keys)
  ...
```
alex: also seeing repeated kvcache growth over long sessions, not reclaimed between user turns. suspecting a leak in our incremental prefill path for streaming chat.
maya: good catch. initial mitigation options: 1) route affected models to quantized fallback (sm-8q) 2) enable kvcache trimming after N tokens 3) soft-rate-limit long sessions at gateway. which is fastest?
jamie: fastest is routing to fallback. awaiting infra API token to flip routing. trimming requires a roll and could break some context fidelity. rate-limit needs gateway change which takes ~15m.
maya: i'll flip routing now to fallback-8q for model-serving-prod/v2. alex, prepare a trimmed-kv rollout in parallel.
ops-bot: @maya issued routing change request: update-route --service model-serving-prod --from v2 --to v2-8q-fallback --weight 100
ops-bot: change accepted, traffic shifting.
alex: confirming: new pods for v2-8q-fallback are healthy. `kubectl get pods -l app=model-serving-prod` shows all Ready=1/1.
jamie: observing immediate drop in restarts on gpu-12. prefill OOM events reduced to 0 in last 2m. good.
support-ps: support wants a short customer note — impact window and mitigation. Drafting: "We observed service instability affecting a subset of long-chat sessions; we routed traffic to a memory-optimized fallback model which restored service. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." Thoughts?
maya: good. add ETA for follow-up: "ETA 4 hours for internal RCA and rollback plan" and mention no data loss.
support-ps: done. sending to CSMs now.
alex: technical next steps: collect heap / KV profiles from before and after, capture perf counters on gpu-12, instrument kvcache trimming behavior. I'll open an internal bug: INF-2026-kv-leak-long-sessions.
jamie: also recommend temporary gateway rule: max_context_tokens=80k for that model until we ship trimmed-kv. lowers risk.
maya: agreed. apply soft rate limit at gateway for model-serving-prod for sessions >80k tokens (enforce 429 with guidance). ops-bot, run `gateway update-rate-limit --service model-serving-prod --max-context 80000 --mode soft`
ops-bot: command queued and executed.
maya: monitoring CPU/GPU mem on gpu-12 and cluster wide. will keep this thread updated.
ops-bot: Customer-impact summary: ~0.6% of requests to model-serving-prod experienced errors or higher latency during the 14:00-14:10 UTC window; majority of users mitigated by fallback routing.
jamie: note for postmortem: include timeline, root cause hypothesis (kvcache not pruning on incremental prefill for long sessions), and mitigation checklist (fallback routing, gateway limits, kvcache trim rollout).
maya: on-call handoff: i'm staying on until 15:30 UTC. if still open, @alex will take 15:30-19:30.
support-ps: customer updates sent. CSMs reporting no escalations so far.
ops-bot: incident status -> mitigated. Pager cleared for on-call.
maya: closing live mitigation — moving to RCA track. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
